full_judgment: 7.2. It, however, appears that the tribunal while adjudicating the contentions raised in the Arpito Sampotti Tribunal Case held, Annexure-B-3, that the petitioners were not entitled to acquire title to the whole of suit land since their vendor, Dhirendra Mohon Dey, had no title to the whole amount of land as there were other co-sharers also as per CS Khatian. We find a specific case to have been demonstrated by the petitioners that Dhirendra Mohon Dey by way of amicable partition owned the suit land in the whole. Admitted publication of SA Khatian Nos. 1948 and 1828 in Dhirendra Mohon's single name including the suit land in its entirety excluding other co-sharers therein appeared to be prima facie evidence of his possession at the relevant time. None of the co-sharers ever challenged the correctness of the SA Khatians or the validity of the family partition as being never done by them. It is evident from the impugned Gazette dated 9-4-2012 that the suit property was enlisted as enemy property vide Case No. 71/6970. Till 1969-70, no other co-sharers came forward to resist the claim of Dhirendra Mohon and to refute sole possession of 48 decimals of CS recorded land in Dhirendra Mohon's name alone. But before the enemy list was done, the SA Khatian got finally published attributing thereto the presumption of possession in Dhirendra Mohon's favour. The incorporation of suit land in SA Khatians in Dhirendra Mohon's name reflects the initial basis of amicable family partition particularly when the Khatians continued to operate till further Khatian under new survey operation was published in ultimate conformity with the earlier Khatians. It appears from the lower court record that a number of co-sharers of Dhirendra Mohon Dey were impleaded as defendants in the Other Classes Suit No. 136 of 1976 which was analogously disposed of with Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1974. None of the co-sharers entered appearance to resist the family partition claim raised by Dhirendra Mohon Dey, rather impliedly allowed by their unopposed acts being ever raised in any legal action whatsoever. Unless a claim is controverted by persons directly affected or likely to be affected thereby, particularly when such claim is adjudicated with opportunities being provided to all concerned, such claim cannot be unilaterally deprecated on a mere hypothesis unattended by necessary surrounding circumstances. The exclusive and continued possession of one co-sharer over the land of other co-sharers for an unobjected and uninterrupted period of 12 years or more creates title by adverse possession in favour of the co-sharer possessing the land of such other co-sharers without material opposition. In the premises, the decision held either by learned erstwhile Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh in the said analogous judgment of Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1974 and Other Classes Suit No. 136 of 1976 or the decision held by the trial tribunal (Annexure-B-3) in Arpito Sampatti Case No. 75 of 2013 or by the appellate tribunal, (Annexure-B-1), in Arpito Appeal No. 02 of 2018, whichever may be, that the basis of SA Khatians in the sole name of Dhirendra Mohon Dey to be absolutely wrong do not appear to us to be in any way logically acceptable.
